title: Interface-Based Priority Queue
story: An emergency room doesn't serve patients in order of arrival — the most critical cases go first, regardless of when they checked in. You need a Priority Queue where items with the highest priority always come out first, no matter when they were added.
why: Priority queues combine generics with interfaces — items must implement Comparable so the queue can always find the highest-priority item.
analogy: Airport boarding groups: First Class boards before Economy, regardless of when they arrived at the gate. The Priority interface is the boarding pass class — it determines who goes first. The priority queue enforces that order.
try_it: Create a `Job` type with `deadline` (Int, smaller = more urgent). Implement Priority where smaller deadline = higher priority. Test by inserting jobs with deadlines 5, 1, 10, 3 and verify pop order is 1, 3, 5, 10.
tips: Use the interface constraint `T: Priority` on both the type AND each method
Insert at the correct position to keep items sorted by priority
pop() from the end of the Vec for O(1) removal of the highest-priority item
common_mistakes: Inserting at the wrong position — items should be in ascending priority order
Using > instead of < when comparing — make sure 'higher than' means what you think
Forgetting the interface bound on method signatures
